x: There are 17 SDGs, with 169 targets, to be met by 2030. The other options are those other numbers.
t: Discriminate 17 goals from 169 targets.

x: Option C is incorrect: the framework is titled 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development', not 2035. It was proposed at Rio+20 (2012).
t: Recall the 2030 Agenda title.

x: No Poverty is Goal 1, Clean Water and Sanitation Goal 6, Climate Action Goal 13, and Partnerships Goal 17. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the SDG numbers.

x: Both are true: NITI Aayog coordinates and monitors the SDGs in India, including the SDG India Index, and the framework is titled 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development'.
t: Recall who tracks the SDGs in India.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: NITI Aayog coordinates and monitors SDG implementation in India.
Statement B: The official SDG framework is titled “Transforming our World: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development”.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: SDG 2 is Zero Hunger, SDG 3 Good Health, SDG 4 Quality Education, and SDG 5 Gender Equality. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the SDG numbers.

x: All four are correct: SDG 7 is clean energy, 8 decent work and growth, 9 industry and infrastructure, and 10 reduced inequalities.
t: Recall the SDG numbers.

x: SDG 11 is sustainable cities, 12 responsible consumption, 14 life below water, and 15 life on land. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Remember: water (14) comes before land (15).

x: Both are true: SDG 15 is Life on Land, and SDG 16 is Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.
t: Recall the SDG numbers.

x: Oilzapper, a mix of bacteria, cleans up oil spills and oily sludge. A microbial fuel cell treats wastewater, and EPR is a producer duty.
t: Match each method to its use.

x: Option B is incorrect: mercury comes under the Minamata Convention. Rotterdam deals with prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides.
t: Match each treaty to its subject.

x: Both are true and R explains A: HFCs replaced ozone-depleting CFCs but trap heat strongly, so the 2016 Kigali Amendment brought them under the Montreal Protocol for phase-down to curb warming.
t: Ask why an ozone treaty would regulate a gas that does not harm ozone.
s:
Assertion (A): The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol provides for the phase-down of HFCs.
Reason (R): HFCs do not deplete the ozone layer but are potent greenhouse gases.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

x: Biodiversity comes under the CBD, biosafety under Cartagena, access and benefit sharing under Nagoya, and plant genetic resources under ITPGRFA. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each subject to its treaty.

x: The order is the Stockholm Declaration (1972), Our Common Future (1987), the Rio Declaration (1992) and the Johannesburg Declaration (2002). The answer is B, D, C, A.
t: Arrange the declarations in time order.

x: I, II and IV are correct: Agenda 21 is the action plan, the Forest Principles cover forests, and the Millennium Declaration set up the MDGs. III is false because 'The Future We Want' came out of Rio+20 in 2012.
t: Match each document to its year.

x: Bioremediation uses naturally occurring organisms to remove pollutants, genetically engineered microbes include the oil-eating superbug, UV kills microbes in water, and pyrolysis breaks waste down without oxygen to recover energy. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each method to its use.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Bioremediation
(b) Genetically engineered microbes
(c) UV purification
(d) Pyrolysis

List-II
(i) Killing microorganisms in drinking water
(ii) Recombinant organisms such as the oil-eating 'superbug'
(iii) Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen to recover energy
(iv) Using naturally occurring organisms to remove pollutants

x: Plasma gasification turns waste into energy with high-temperature plasma, bio-asphalt replaces petroleum asphalt, hydrogen powers fuel cells that emit only water, and biofuels such as ethanol and biodiesel come from biomass. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each method to its use.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Plasma gasification
(b) Bio-asphalt
(c) Hydrogen fuel
(d) Biofuels

List-II
(i) Ethanol and biodiesel made from biomass
(ii) Used in fuel cells that emit only water vapour
(iii) Alternative to petroleum-based asphalt
(iv) Waste-to-energy using very high-temperature plasma

x: Both are true: a green muffler (a tree belt) reduces noise and some air pollution, and Euro/BS norms control vehicle emissions. They are separate measures, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two separate measures explain each other.

x: Renewable energy tackles fossil-fuel pollution by replacing coal and oil. The other options deal with waste or water.
t: Match each method to its use.

x: All four pairs are correct: landfill for disposal, incineration for burning, vermicomposting with worms, and bioremediation with microbes.
t: Check each pair.

x: Heritage comes under the World Heritage Convention, the climate framework is the UNFCCC, binding targets for developed countries came with the Kyoto Protocol, and the 1.5°C goal is from Paris. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each subject to its treaty.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Natural and cultural heritage
(b) Climate change framework
(c) Binding emission targets for developed countries
(d) Climate action and the 1.5°C goal

List-II
(i) Paris Agreement
(ii) World Heritage Convention
(iii) Kyoto Protocol
(iv) UNFCCC

x: Ozone comes under the Vienna Convention, phasing out ODS under the Montreal Protocol, hazardous waste under Basel, and the human environment under the Stockholm Declaration. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Discriminate Vienna (framework) from Montreal (phase-out).

x: All three are correct: the Stockholm Declaration came from the first major UN environment conference, on the human environment, and 'Our Common Future' is the Brundtland Report.
t: Recall the Stockholm and Brundtland documents.

x: Our Common Future (1987) defined sustainable development, the Rio Declaration set out 27 principles, Agenda 21 is the action plan for the 21st century, and the Forest Principles are a non-binding statement on forests. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Identify each document by what it uniquely contains.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Our Common Future
(b) Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
(c) Agenda 21
(d) Forest Principles

List-II
(i) Defined sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations
(ii) 27 principles on environment and development
(iii) Comprehensive action plan for the 21st century
(iv) Non-binding statement on the sustainable management of forests

x: Both are true: the Johannesburg Declaration came from the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development and focused on putting commitments into practice.
t: Recall the Johannesburg summit.

x: All three are correct: the Millennium Declaration came in 2000, and the 2030 Agenda, with its 17 SDGs, was adopted in 2015.
t: Arrange the development agendas in time order.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Millennium Declaration was issued in 2000.
II. The 2030 Agenda was adopted in 2015.
III. The 2030 Agenda contains 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
